variables.label: Carbon monoxide in the air (smoke)
variables.aggregation: mean of pixels with qa_value>0.5
variables.notes: Dominated by biomass burning in the dry season. Monthly value = mean of all quality-filtered pixels in county from 4 (2018-04..2018-12: 6) evenly spaced sampled orbits (not all ~45 overpasses) - noisy, cloud-affected in wet season. Starts 2018-04/07 (S5P operational data begins mid-2018), so the 2018 baseline is partial.
variables.source: Copernicus Sentinel-5P TROPOMI L2 (OFFL/RPRO) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.native_resolution: 5.5 x 3.5 km (7 x 3.5 km before Aug 2019)
variables.plain: Amount of carbon monoxide in the air column, a gas released mostly by grass and bush fires in the dry season. Higher = more smoke.
variables.method: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI total column, mean of quality-filtered pixels from 4 sampled orbits per month.
variables.caution: Only a few satellite passes sampled per month; noisy and cloud-affected in the wet season.

variables.label: Dust and smoke index (UV aerosol index)
variables.aggregation: mean of pixels with qa_value>0.8
variables.notes: Positive = absorbing aerosol (Saharan dust, biomass-burning smoke); can be negative. Monthly value = mean of all quality-filtered pixels in county from 4 (2018-04..2018-12: 6) evenly spaced sampled orbits (not all ~45 overpasses) - noisy, cloud-affected in wet season. Starts 2018-04/07 (S5P operational data begins mid-2018), so the 2018 baseline is partial.
variables.source: Copernicus Sentinel-5P TROPOMI L2 (OFFL/RPRO) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.native_resolution: 5.5 x 3.5 km (7 x 3.5 km before Aug 2019)
variables.plain: Detects light-absorbing particles such as desert dust and smoke. Positive values = dust or smoke present; values near or below zero = clean air or clouds.
variables.method: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI UV aerosol index, mean of quality-filtered pixels from 4 sampled orbits per month.
variables.how_to_read: Above 0 = dust or smoke present; can be negative.
variables.caution: Only a few satellite passes sampled per month; noisy.

variables.label: Haze from coarse dust (aerosols, 840 nm)
variables.source: CERES SYN1deg via NASA POWER (parameter AOD_84)
variables.aggregation: value of the POWER grid cell containing the county centroid (centroid sampling; grid cells are ~county-sized or larger)
variables.notes: Longer-wavelength AOD; relatively more sensitive to coarse dust than to smoke.
variables.plain: How hazy the air is, measured at a longer wavelength that responds more to coarse dust than to smoke.
variables.method: Aerosol optical depth at 840 nm, CERES SYN1deg via NASA POWER; county-centre grid cell (~110 km).
variables.caution: Very coarse grid (about 110 km), so neighbouring counties often share one value.

variables.label: Haze from dust and smoke (aerosols)
variables.source: CERES SYN1deg via NASA POWER (parameter AOD_55)
variables.aggregation: value of the POWER grid cell containing the county centroid (centroid sampling; grid cells are ~county-sized or larger)
variables.notes: Column aerosol optical depth; high values in the dry season reflect Saharan dust and biomass burning.
variables.plain: How hazy the air is from dust, smoke and other particles. Dry-season peaks come from Saharan dust and grass burning.
variables.method: Aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, CERES SYN1deg via NASA POWER; value of the ~110 km grid cell at the county centre.
variables.caution: Very coarse grid (about 110 km), so neighbouring counties often share one value.

variables.label: Nitrogen dioxide in the air (NO2)
variables.aggregation: mean of pixels with qa_value>0.75
variables.notes: Near detection limit away from towns/fires (county means can be <=0, so index_ok false); dry-season peaks from biomass burning. Monthly value = mean of all quality-filtered pixels in county from 4 (2018-04..2018-12: 6) evenly spaced sampled orbits (not all ~45 overpasses) - noisy, cloud-affected in wet season. Starts 2018-04/07 (S5P operational data begins mid-2018), so the 2018 baseline is partial.
variables.source: Copernicus Sentinel-5P TROPOMI L2 (OFFL/RPRO) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.native_resolution: 5.5 x 3.5 km (7 x 3.5 km before Aug 2019)
variables.plain: Amount of nitrogen dioxide, a pollutant from burning (fires, engines, gas flaring). Mostly near zero except near towns, fires and oil fields.
variables.method: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI tropospheric NO2, mean of quality-filtered pixels from 4 sampled orbits per month.
variables.caution: Near the satellite's detection limit across most of the country; county values can be zero or negative.

variables.label: Dryness of the air (vapour pressure deficit)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS
variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of 1/24° cells (cell coverage fraction x cos lat)
variables.notes: Atmospheric dryness; high VPD stresses crops. Coverage 2018-01..2025-12.
variables.plain: How 'thirsty' the air is: the gap between how much moisture the air holds and how much it could hold. High values dry out crops and pasture.
variables.method: TerraClimate vapour pressure deficit, kPa.
variables.how_to_read: Higher = drier, more stressful air for plants and livestock.

variables.label: Sunshine (incoming solar radiation)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS
variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of 1/24° cells (cell coverage fraction x cos lat)
variables.plain: How much sunlight reaches the ground. Lower in the cloudy rainy season, higher in the dry season.
variables.method: TerraClimate downward shortwave radiation, W/m2.

variables.label: Amphibian species (frogs, toads)
variables.aggregation: county mean of 10 km richness cells
variables.notes: IUCN range-map based (Dec 2017).
variables.source: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013; IUCN + BirdLife range maps, 2017-2019 versions)
variables.plain: Average number of amphibian species whose known range covers this county. Higher = richer wildlife.
variables.method: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013) from IUCN / BirdLife range maps; mean species per 10 km cell.
variables.caution: Based on where species could live (range maps), not field sightings.

variables.label: Animal species (amphibians, birds, mammals)
variables.aggregation: sum of the three county means
variables.notes: Reptiles not included (not in the downloadable package). Range-map richness = potential, not observed, species.
variables.source: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013; IUCN + BirdLife range maps, 2017-2019 versions)
variables.plain: Average number of amphibian, bird and mammal species whose known range covers this county. Reptiles are not included.
variables.method: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013) from IUCN / BirdLife range maps; mean species per 10 km cell.
variables.caution: Based on where species could live (range maps), not field sightings.

variables.label: Bird species
variables.aggregation: county mean of 10 km richness cells
variables.notes: BirdLife range maps v7, excl. seabirds.
variables.source: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013; IUCN + BirdLife range maps, 2017-2019 versions)
variables.plain: Average number of bird species whose known range covers this county. Higher = richer wildlife.
variables.method: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013) from IUCN / BirdLife range maps; mean species per 10 km cell.
variables.caution: Based on where species could live (range maps), not field sightings.

variables.label: Mammal species
variables.aggregation: county mean of 10 km richness cells
variables.notes: IUCN range maps (Mar 2018).
variables.source: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013; IUCN + BirdLife range maps, 2017-2019 versions)
variables.plain: Average number of mammal species whose known range covers this county. Higher = richer wildlife.
variables.method: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013) from IUCN / BirdLife range maps; mean species per 10 km cell.
variables.caution: Based on where species could live (range maps), not field sightings.

variables.label: Threatened bird species
variables.aggregation: county mean
variables.notes: IUCN threatened categories.
variables.source: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013; IUCN + BirdLife range maps, 2017-2019 versions)
variables.plain: Average number of threatened (IUCN red-list) bird species whose range covers this county.
variables.method: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013) from IUCN / BirdLife range maps; mean species per 10 km cell.
variables.caution: Based on where species could live (range maps), not field sightings.

variables.label: Threatened mammal species
variables.aggregation: county mean
variables.notes: IUCN threatened categories.
variables.source: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013; IUCN + BirdLife range maps, 2017-2019 versions)
variables.plain: Average number of threatened (IUCN red-list) mammal species whose range covers this county.
variables.method: BiodiversityMapping.org (Jenkins, Pimm & Joppa 2013) from IUCN / BirdLife range maps; mean species per 10 km cell.
variables.caution: Based on where species could live (range maps), not field sightings.

variables.aggregation: county mean as computed in Drive pipeline (POWER grid cells averaged over county)
variables.label: 3-month drought index (SPEI, satellite rain)
variables.source: Derived: IMERG precipitation minus Thornthwaite PET, 3-month SPEI vs county 2000-2026 history
variables.notes: Below -1 = dry, above +1 = wet. Not ratio-indexable (can be <= 0).
variables.plain: Takes rainfall minus potential evaporation over the last three months and compares it with the same three-month window in every year of the county's 2000–2026 record. The difference is given in standard deviations: 0 is normal and negative values are drier than normal.
variables.method: SPEI-3 from IMERG precipitation minus Thornthwaite PET (MERRA-2 temperature), county series 2000-2026.
variables.caution: The baseline is short and the evaporation formula is simple. Check it against the combined drought index where you can.

variables.label: 3-month drought index (TerraClimate)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 ppt and PET (Penman-Monteith)
variables.aggregation: county-mean P-PET, 3-month sum, log-logistic SPEI vs 1991-2020
variables.notes: TerraClimate precipitation is ~40% below IMERG in 2018-2025 and its recent years are anomalously dry relative to 1991-2020 (it inherits ERA5/CRU trends), so this member is biased toward drought.
variables.plain: Compares the last three months of rain minus evaporation with normal for that county and season.
variables.method: SPEI-3 from TerraClimate precipitation minus Penman-Monteith PET, log-logistic fit, 1991-2020 baseline.
variables.caution: TerraClimate rain is ~40% below other products after 2018, so this index leans toward drought.

variables.label: 3-month rainfall index (CHIRPS)
variables.source: CHIRPS v3.0 monthly, UCSB CHC
variables.aggregation: county-mean rainfall, 3-month sum, gamma SPI vs 1991-2020
variables.notes: Gamma distribution with zero-rain probability per county and calendar month; dry-season months with near-zero rain give unstable SPI (bounded to +-3.09).
variables.plain: Compares the last three months of rain with what is normal for that county and season. Below zero = less rain than usual.
variables.method: SPI-3 from CHIRPS v3.0, gamma fit with zero-rain probability, 1991-2020 baseline, capped at +/-3.09.
variables.caution: Unstable in dry-season months when almost no rain falls.

variables.label: Drought index (combined, best estimate)
variables.source: Ensemble of 4 drought indices: SPEI-3 IMERG/MERRA-2 (drive_climate spei3), SPI-3 CHIRPS v3.0, SPEI-3 TerraClimate, TerraClimate PDSI standardised (scripts/drought_ensemble.py)
variables.aggregation: mean of >=3 available member indices
variables.notes: Mean of standardised 3-month drought indices from independent rainfall inputs (satellite IMERG, gauge-blended CHIRPS, reanalysis-driven TerraClimate). <-1 moderate, <-1.5 severe drought. Members use different baselines (TerraClimate/CHIRPS 1991-2020; IMERG SPEI 2000-2026). Pooled 2018-2025 county-month correlations between members: CHIRPS SPI vs IMERG SPEI r=0.39, CHIRPS SPI vs TC SPEI r=0.34, IMERG SPEI vs TC SPEI r=0.31, TC SPEI vs TC PDSI-z r=0.45.
variables.plain: Our main drought measure: the average of four drought indices built from different rain data.
variables.method: Ensemble of IMERG SPEI-3, CHIRPS SPI-3, TerraClimate SPEI-3 and re-standardised TerraClimate PDSI. At least 3 members required; values in standard deviations.
variables.how_to_read: Below -1 = moderate drought, below -1.5 = severe; above +1 = unusually wet
variables.caution: Leans slightly dry because the TerraClimate members are dry-biased. Trust a drought only when members agree and spread is low.

variables.label: Drought sources in agreement (share)
variables.source: Ensemble of 4 drought indices: SPEI-3 IMERG/MERRA-2 (drive_climate spei3), SPI-3 CHIRPS v3.0, SPEI-3 TerraClimate, TerraClimate PDSI standardised (scripts/drought_ensemble.py)
variables.aggregation: share of members with same sign as mean
variables.notes: 1 = all members agree whether the county is drier or wetter than normal.
variables.plain: Share of the four drought indices that agree on whether the county is drier or wetter than normal. 1 = all agree.
variables.method: Share of ensemble members with the same sign as the ensemble mean (0-1).
variables.how_to_read: 1 = all sources agree; 0.5 = sources split

variables.label: Drought uncertainty (how much sources disagree)
variables.source: Ensemble of 4 drought indices: SPEI-3 IMERG/MERRA-2 (drive_climate spei3), SPI-3 CHIRPS v3.0, SPEI-3 TerraClimate, TerraClimate PDSI standardised (scripts/drought_ensemble.py)
variables.aggregation: sample standard deviation across members
variables.notes: How much the drought indices disagree. <0.5: inputs agree; >1: the sign or severity of the anomaly depends on which rainfall product you trust (typical in the Sudd and Upper Nile, where there are almost no rain gauges). Pooled 2018-2025 county-month correlations between members: CHIRPS SPI vs IMERG SPEI r=0.39, CHIRPS SPI vs TC SPEI r=0.34, IMERG SPEI vs TC SPEI r=0.31, TC SPEI vs TC PDSI-z r=0.45.
variables.plain: How much the four drought indices disagree for this county and month. Low = the rain datasets agree; high = the answer depends on which dataset you trust.
variables.method: Standard deviation across the four drought-ensemble members.
variables.how_to_read: Below 0.5 = sources agree; above 1 = sources disagree strongly (common in the Sudd and Upper Nile)

variables.label: Drought uncertainty (range between sources)
variables.source: Ensemble of 4 drought indices: SPEI-3 IMERG/MERRA-2 (drive_climate spei3), SPI-3 CHIRPS v3.0, SPEI-3 TerraClimate, TerraClimate PDSI standardised (scripts/drought_ensemble.py)
variables.aggregation: max - min across members
variables.notes: Alternative uncertainty measure to the spread.
variables.label_original: Drought index range (max - min of members)
variables.plain: Gap between the wettest and driest of the four drought indices. Larger = less certain whether the county is dry or wet.
variables.method: Maximum minus minimum across the four drought-ensemble members (SD units).

variables.label: Long-term drought (Palmer index, adjusted)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 PDSI
variables.aggregation: county-mean PDSI, z-score vs the county's 1991-2020 values for the same calendar month
variables.notes: PDSI has long memory (~9-12 months) so it lags SPI/SPEI-3; it shares the TerraClimate precipitation with dr_spei3_tc, so these two members are not independent.
variables.plain: A slow-moving drought index that reflects the past 9-12 months of rain and heat, rescaled so 0 = normal for that county and month.
variables.method: TerraClimate PDSI z-scored per county and calendar month vs 1991-2020. Drought-ensemble member.
variables.caution: Uses TerraClimate rain, which is dry-biased after 2018; shares that input with the TerraClimate SPEI.

variables.label: Palmer drought index (raw)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS
variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of 1/24° cells (cell coverage fraction x cos lat)
variables.notes: Negative = drought. Not ratio-indexable. TerraClimate PDSI is strongly negative across South Sudan in 2018-2025 (country mean ~ -6.6) because its ERA5-driven precipitation is well below its 1991-2020 climatology; treat as relative, and cross-check with IMERG-based spei3. Coverage 2018-01..2025-12.
variables.plain: A classic long-term drought index. Negative = drought, positive = wet. In this dataset values sit far below zero every year, even in flood years.
variables.method: TerraClimate v1.1 Palmer Drought Severity Index (scale about -4 dry to +4 wet).
variables.how_to_read: Compare places, not absolute values
variables.caution: Reads about -5 to -8 every year, including the 2020 flood year: a dry bias in the input rain. Use the combined drought index instead.

variables.label: Number of extreme-weather flags
variables.notes: Sum of tc_extreme_wet, tc_extreme_dry, tc_extreme_heat. County-mean value compared with the same county's 1991-2020 TerraClimate climatology for the same calendar month (empirical percentile over 30 years). 1 = extreme, 0 = not. 2018-2025 is drier and hotter than 1991-2020 in TerraClimate, so dry/heat flags fire ~30% of months and wet ~4%.
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS; percentiles computed by team
variables.aggregation: flag on county-mean series
variables.plain: How many of three extremes (very wet, very dry, very hot) happened in the county that month, from 0 to 3.
variables.method: Sum of the TerraClimate extreme wet, dry and heat flags vs 1991-2020 county percentiles.
variables.how_to_read: 0 = no extremes, 3 = wet, dry and hot extremes at once (rare)
variables.caution: Dry and heat flags fire too often because TerraClimate leans dry and hot after 2018.

variables.label: Unusually dry month (flag)
variables.notes: Precipitation below the 10th percentile; never flagged in months whose 10th pct is 0 (normal dry season). County-mean value compared with the same county's 1991-2020 TerraClimate climatology for the same calendar month (empirical percentile over 30 years). 1 = extreme, 0 = not. 2018-2025 is drier and hotter than 1991-2020 in TerraClimate, so dry/heat flags fire ~30% of months and wet ~4%.
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS; percentiles computed by team
variables.aggregation: flag on county-mean series
variables.plain: Marks months when rainfall was in the driest 10% for that county and month of the year, compared with 1991-2020. Never set in normally rainless months.
variables.method: TerraClimate precipitation below the county's 1991-2020 10th percentile for that calendar month.
variables.how_to_read: 1 = extreme month, 0 = normal
variables.caution: Fires far too often (~30% of months) because TerraClimate rain is dry-biased after 2018.

variables.label: Unusually hot month (flag)
variables.notes: Mean daily max temperature above the 90th percentile. County-mean value compared with the same county's 1991-2020 TerraClimate climatology for the same calendar month (empirical percentile over 30 years). 1 = extreme, 0 = not. 2018-2025 is drier and hotter than 1991-2020 in TerraClimate, so dry/heat flags fire ~30% of months and wet ~4%.
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS; percentiles computed by team
variables.aggregation: flag on county-mean series
variables.plain: Marks months when daytime highs were in the hottest 10% for that county and month of the year, compared with 1991-2020.
variables.method: TerraClimate monthly mean daily max temperature above the county's 1991-2020 90th percentile for that calendar month.
variables.how_to_read: 1 = extreme month, 0 = normal
variables.caution: TerraClimate's recent years run hotter and drier than its own 1991-2020 baseline, so this flag fires in ~30% of months.

variables.label: Unusually wet month (flag)
variables.notes: Precipitation above the 90th percentile. County-mean value compared with the same county's 1991-2020 TerraClimate climatology for the same calendar month (empirical percentile over 30 years). 1 = extreme, 0 = not. 2018-2025 is drier and hotter than 1991-2020 in TerraClimate, so dry/heat flags fire ~30% of months and wet ~4%.
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS; percentiles computed by team
variables.aggregation: flag on county-mean series
variables.plain: Marks months when rainfall was in the wettest 10% for that county and month of the year, compared with 1991-2020.
variables.method: TerraClimate precipitation above the county's 1991-2020 90th percentile for that calendar month.
variables.how_to_read: 1 = extreme month, 0 = normal
variables.caution: Fires rarely (~4% of months) because TerraClimate rain is dry-biased after 2018.

variables.label: Active fires detected (MODIS)
variables.source: MODIS MOD14A1/MYD14A1 v061 (Terra+Aqua daily 1 km FireMask) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.aggregation: count of daily 1 km fire pixels (FireMask 7-9, all confidence levels) inside county, summed over Terra and Aqua and all days of the month
variables.notes: Months with incomplete Terra/Aqua daily coverage on Planetary Computer are scaled to a full month (count x expected/available sensor-days; e.g. 2022-12 had 38/62); months with <50% coverage are dropped (2025-07..2025-11 missing from the PC catalogue). Comparable to FIRMS MODIS counts (FIRMS API not reachable from build env). Strongly seasonal (dry season Nov-Mar). index_ok false because many county-months are 0.
variables.plain: Number of fire detections seen by NASA's MODIS satellites in the month. Fires are mostly grass and bush burning in the dry season (Nov-Mar).
variables.method: MODIS MOD14A1/MYD14A1 daily 1 km fire mask, Terra + Aqua; months with partial coverage scaled up, <50% coverage dropped.
variables.caution: Jul-Nov 2025 missing. Prefer the VIIRS fire count, which sees smaller fires.

variables.label: Active fires detected (VIIRS)
variables.source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP 375 m, standard processing (VIIRS_SNPP_SP)
variables.aggregation: count of detections; nominal/high confidence only (low excluded), type 0 = presumed vegetation fire (static sources such as oil-field gas flares excluded), detection point inside county
variables.notes: Single sensor (Suomi-NPP) for the whole 2018-2025 series so trends are consistent. Strongly seasonal (dry season Nov-Mar), zero in most wet-season months. Versus MODIS fire_count (fire_pipeline.py, same months): pooled county-month Pearson r = 0.982, Spearman = 0.969, national monthly r = 0.988, median per-county r = 0.975; VIIRS detects 1.45x as many fires as MODIS (finer 375 m pixels see small fires). Per-county table: data/processed/validation/viirs_vs_modis_fire.csv.
variables.plain: Number of fire detections in the month from the VIIRS satellite sensor. Fires peak in the dry season (November to March).
variables.method: NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP 375 m, one sensor for 2018-2025. Detects ~1.45x as many fires as MODIS (r = 0.98).

variables.label: Active fires detected (VIIRS, NOAA-20)
variables.source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS NOAA-20 375 m, standard processing
variables.aggregation: count of detections; nominal/high confidence only (low excluded), type 0 = presumed vegetation fire (static sources such as oil-field gas flares excluded), detection point inside county
variables.notes: 2020-2025 only; reported separately (not mixed into the S-NPP trend series). NOAA-20 vs S-NPP county-month r = 0.998, NOAA-20/S-NPP total ratio = 0.97.
variables.plain: Number of fire detections from the NOAA-20 satellite, which sees fires as small as a few hundred metres. Available from 2020 only.
variables.method: NASA FIRMS VIIRS NOAA-20 375 m, standard processing. Nearly identical to the S-NPP series (r = 0.998).
variables.caution: Starts in 2020; use the S-NPP VIIRS series for 2018-2025 trends.

variables.label: Burned area
variables.source: MODIS MCD64A1 v061 burned area via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.aggregation: sum of burned 500 m pixels (Burn_Date>0) x pixel area (sinusoidal equal-area, 0.2147 km2)
variables.notes: Monthly burned area; zero in most wet-season months. Months absent from the Planetary Computer catalogue (no rows, no PNG): 2023-09, 2024-07, 2025-05, 2025-08, 2025-09, 2025-10.
variables.plain: Area of land that burned during the month, in square kilometres. Mostly dry-season grass fires; usually zero in the rainy months.
variables.method: MODIS MCD64A1 v061 monthly burned area.
variables.caution: Some months are missing from the data source (e.g. 2023-09, 2024-07, 2025-05, 2025-08 to 2025-10).

variables.label: Burned area (% of county)
variables.source: MODIS MCD64A1 v061 burned area via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.aggregation: burned pixels / all pixels in county x 100
variables.plain: Share of the county's land that burned during the month. Mostly dry-season grass fires; usually zero in the rainy months.
variables.method: MODIS MCD64A1 v061 monthly burned area divided by county area.
variables.caution: Some months are missing from the data source (e.g. 2023-09, 2024-07, 2025-05, 2025-08 to 2025-10).

variables.label: Fire intensity (VIIRS)
variables.source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP 375 m, standard processing (VIIRS_SNPP_SP)
variables.aggregation: sum of per-detection FRP; nominal/high confidence only (low excluded), type 0 = presumed vegetation fire (static sources such as oil-field gas flares excluded), detection point inside county
variables.notes: Sum of instantaneous FRP at overpass time; a proxy for fire intensity x extent.
variables.plain: Total heat given off by fires detected in the month, a rough measure of how much and how intensely land burned.
variables.method: Sum of instantaneous fire radiative power (MW) of S-NPP VIIRS 375 m detections at overpass time.

variables.label: Fire intensity (VIIRS, NOAA-20)
variables.source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS NOAA-20 375 m, standard processing
variables.aggregation: sum of per-detection FRP; nominal/high confidence only (low excluded), type 0 = presumed vegetation fire (static sources such as oil-field gas flares excluded), detection point inside county
variables.plain: Total heat given off by fires detected in the month, a rough measure of how big and intense the fires were. Available from 2020 only.
variables.method: Sum of fire radiative power (MW) of NOAA-20 VIIRS 375 m detections at overpass time.
variables.caution: Starts in 2020.

variables.label: Bare ground (% of county)
variables.source: Esri / Impact Observatory 10 m Annual Land Use Land Cover (io-lulc-annual-v02, Sentinel-2) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.native_resolution: 10 m (sampled at 80 m via COG overview)
variables.aggregation: class pixels / all classified pixels (excl. no-data, cloud) x 100; nearest-neighbour systematic 1-in-64 sample of the 10 m map
variables.notes: Annual product dated YYYY-07-01, years 2017-2023 (2024+ not on Planetary Computer). Year-to-year changes partly reflect classifier differences; flooded vegetation and water shares react to the 2019-2022 floods.
variables.plain: Share of the county that is bare soil, rock or sand with little or no plant cover, from yearly satellite land maps.
variables.method: Esri / Impact Observatory 10 m annual land cover from Sentinel-2 (2017-2023); share of county pixels.
variables.caution: Annual, 2017-2023 only. Some year-to-year change comes from classifier differences, not real change.

variables.label: Built-up area (% of county)
variables.source: Esri / Impact Observatory 10 m Annual Land Use Land Cover (io-lulc-annual-v02, Sentinel-2) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.native_resolution: 10 m (sampled at 80 m via COG overview)
variables.aggregation: class pixels / all classified pixels (excl. no-data, cloud) x 100; nearest-neighbour systematic 1-in-64 sample of the 10 m map
variables.notes: Annual product dated YYYY-07-01, years 2017-2023 (2024+ not on Planetary Computer). Year-to-year changes partly reflect classifier differences; flooded vegetation and water shares react to the 2019-2022 floods.
variables.plain: Share of the county covered by buildings, roads and other built structures, from yearly satellite land maps.
variables.method: Esri / Impact Observatory 10 m annual land cover from Sentinel-2 (2017-2023); share of county pixels.
variables.caution: Yearly, 2017-2023 only. Part of the change from year to year comes from differences in how the maps were classified.

variables.label: Cropland (% of county)
variables.source: Esri / Impact Observatory 10 m Annual Land Use Land Cover (io-lulc-annual-v02, Sentinel-2) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.native_resolution: 10 m (sampled at 80 m via COG overview)

variables.source: MODIS MOD13A1 + MYD13A1 v061 via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.aggregation: per-pixel monthly maximum of 16-day composites (Terra+Aqua, pixel reliability good/marginal), then mean of valid ~1 km cells in county

variables.label: Vegetation greenness (NDVI, 1 km monthly)

variables.label: Soil moisture, top 1 m (NASA SMAP)
variables.source: SMAP L4 SPL4SMGP v008 (3-hourly, 9 km) via Google Earth Engine (NASA/SMAP/SPL4SMGP/008; years 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025)
variables.aggregation: per-cell monthly mean of 3-hourly values, then county mean
variables.notes: Model-assimilation estimate for 0-100 cm; smoother and lagged relative to surface soil moisture. Monthly means of the 3-hourly fields computed in Earth Engine (scripts/gee_smap.py).
variables.plain: How wet the top metre of soil is, which is where crop and pasture roots draw water. Given as the share of the soil volume that is water (0.30 = 30%).
variables.method: NASA SMAP Level-4 (SPL4SMGP v008): SMAP satellite microwave readings combined with NASA's GEOS land model every 3 hours on a 9 km grid; averaged to months, then to counties.
variables.caution: A model estimate guided by satellite readings; the top metre is not measured directly. Cells are 9 km across, so small wetlands blur together.

variables.label: Surface soil moisture, top 5 cm (NASA SMAP)
variables.source: SMAP L4 SPL4SMGP v008 (3-hourly, 9 km, NASA GEOS land model + SMAP brightness-temperature assimilation) via Google Earth Engine (NASA/SMAP/SPL4SMGP/008; years 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025)
variables.aggregation: per-cell monthly mean of 3-hourly values, then mean of ~1 km cells (nearest 9 km cell) in county
variables.notes: Model-assimilation product (gap-free), not a direct retrieval; L4 surface layer is 0-5 cm. Monthly means of the 3-hourly fields computed in Earth Engine (scripts/gee_smap.py).
variables.plain: How wet the top 5 cm of soil is, as the share of the soil volume that is water. It reacts to rain within days.
variables.method: NASA SMAP Level-4 (SPL4SMGP v008), 3-hourly, 9 km; averaged to months, then to counties.
variables.caution: Changes quickly after each rain. The 1 m layer is a better guide to drought.

variables.label: Water evaporated by land and plants (monthly)
variables.source: MODIS MOD16A2GF v061 (Terra, 8-day, gap-filled) via NASA AppEEARS
variables.aggregation: 8-day ET totals prorated to calendar months by day overlap (last composite of each year is 5/6 days), per ~1 km cell; then mean of valid cells in county
variables.notes: Actual ET (Penman-Monteith MOD16). Open water, urban and barren pixels are fill and excluded (e.g. the permanent Sudd open water), so wetland counties are under-represented. Cells need >=75% of month's days valid. Annual sums vs MOD16A3GF modis_et_mm: r=1.0, ratio 0.9999. AppEEARS area request clipped to the South Sudan outline, geographic projection.
variables.plain: Water that evaporated from soil and plants during the month, in millimetres.
variables.method: MODIS MOD16A2GF v061 8-day gap-filled ET (Penman-Monteith), summed to months via AppEEARS.
variables.caution: Open water, towns and bare land are left out, so swamp counties such as those in the Sudd are under-represented.

variables.label: Water evaporated by land and plants (yearly)
variables.source: MODIS MOD16A3GF v061 (gap-filled annual) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.aggregation: mean of valid cells in county
variables.notes: Planetary Computer only hosts the annual MOD16A3GF (no 8-day MOD16A2), so ET is annual (date = YYYY-07-01). Open water, urban and barren pixels are fill in MOD16 and excluded (e.g. permanent Sudd open water).
variables.plain: Total water that evaporated from soil and plants over the year, in millimetres. Higher = wetter, greener land using more water.
variables.method: MODIS MOD16A3GF v061 annual gap-filled evapotranspiration (500 m).
variables.caution: Open water, towns and bare land are excluded, so swamp counties such as the Sudd are under-represented.

variables.label: Flooded area (% of county, radar)
variables.aggregation: flooded area / known area x 100
variables.notes: Radar (C-band SAR) change detection on a ~440 m grid (10 m scenes read at 160 m, block-averaged): a pixel is FLOODED when its monthly mean VV-VH ratio is > 3.0 dB above its own dry-season reference (median of the March means 2018-2025) - water under grass/papyrus/rice produces a double bounce that brightens VV much more than VH; OPEN WATER = VV < -18 and VH < -24 dB. Sees through cloud (unlike MODIS) and sees water under vegetation, which is most of the Sudd flood. It measures inundation BEYOND the normal dry-season state: permanent swamp is part of the reference and is not counted, so values are near 0 in the dry season. Validated on 4-8 Oct 2022 UNOSAT (new flood vs March 2022: F1 0.59, area ratio 0.95; see docs/CLIMATE_DATA_DECISIONS.md). Revisit 6-12 days 2018-2021, 12-24 days after Sentinel-1B failed (Dec 2021) until Sentinel-1C (2025): pixels without an acquisition inherit the previous month (max 2); county-months with <50% known area dropped.
variables.source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 A/B IW GRD, radiometrically terrain-corrected (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.label_original: Flooded area (% of county, Sentinel-1 radar)
variables.plain: Share of the county newly under water compared with its normal dry-season state. Mapped by a radar satellite that sees through cloud and under grass.
variables.method: Sentinel-1 C-band radar change detection: monthly VV-VH more than 3 dB above the pixel's March reference (~440 m grid).
variables.caution: The radar flood map is reliable from July to November. In the dry season it misses flooded vegetation and receding water, and in Bor South it disagrees with MODIS. For all seasons, use the MODIS water or Sudd layer.

variables.label: Flooded area (radar)
variables.aggregation: flooded share of known area x county area
variables.notes: Radar (C-band SAR) change detection on a ~440 m grid (10 m scenes read at 160 m, block-averaged): a pixel is FLOODED when its monthly mean VV-VH ratio is > 3.0 dB above its own dry-season reference (median of the March means 2018-2025) - water under grass/papyrus/rice produces a double bounce that brightens VV much more than VH; OPEN WATER = VV < -18 and VH < -24 dB. Sees through cloud (unlike MODIS) and sees water under vegetation, which is most of the Sudd flood. It measures inundation BEYOND the normal dry-season state: permanent swamp is part of the reference and is not counted, so values are near 0 in the dry season. Validated on 4-8 Oct 2022 UNOSAT (new flood vs March 2022: F1 0.59, area ratio 0.95; see docs/CLIMATE_DATA_DECISIONS.md). Revisit 6-12 days 2018-2021, 12-24 days after Sentinel-1B failed (Dec 2021) until Sentinel-1C (2025): pixels without an acquisition inherit the previous month (max 2); county-months with <50% known area dropped. index_ok false: dry-season months and many 2018 months are ~0.
variables.source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 A/B IW GRD, radiometrically terrain-corrected (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Area newly under water compared with the normal dry-season state, in square kilometres, mapped by radar satellite that sees through cloud and under grass.
variables.method: Sentinel-1 C-band radar change detection: monthly VV-VH more than 3 dB above the pixel's March reference (~440 m grid).
variables.caution: Radar flood map is reliable Jul-Nov; it misses flooded vegetation and receding water in the dry season and disagrees with MODIS in Bor South. Use MODIS water / Sudd layer for all-season.

variables.label: Flooded land near oil wells and fields
variables.aggregation: flooded area within 5 km of any oil well / field point
variables.notes: Oil-pollution spread proxy for Unity, Ruweng and Upper Nile oil fields (Thar Jath, Unity, Toma South, Paloich/Adar...), where produced-water pits, leaking flowlines and spills have been documented (e.g. Sign of Hope / Hoffnungszeichen field studies 2014-2019 in Unity and Ruweng). Only counties with oil infrastructure have values; OSM well locations are incomplete. Exposure, not measured contamination: no open county-level water-quality data exist for South Sudan. Flood = Sentinel-1 flooded class (VV-VH rise >3 dB over the March reference; reliable Jul-Nov, under-detects receding Dec-Jun water).
variables.source: Derived: Sentinel-1 flood (flood_s1_pipeline.py) x WorldPop R2025A 1 km / oil wells & fields (OSM, GEM GOGET); scripts/flood_exposure.py
variables.label_original: Flooded area near oil wells/fields (5 km)
variables.plain: Area of flood water within 5 km of mapped oil wells and fields, in square kilometres. A warning sign for possible spread of oil pollution, not a measure of it.
variables.method: Sentinel-1 flood class within 5 km of OSM wells and GEM GOGET oil fields (Unity, Ruweng, Upper Nile).
variables.caution: Exposure only: no open water-quality data exist. Radar flood map misses dry-season water.

variables.label: Oil wells/fields reached by flood water
variables.aggregation: count of oil well/field points with a flooded cell within ~1 km
variables.notes: See flood_oilfield_exposure_km2. Exposure, not measured contamination: no open county-level water-quality data exist for South Sudan. Flood = Sentinel-1 flooded class (VV-VH rise >3 dB over the March reference; reliable Jul-Nov, under-detects receding Dec-Jun water).
variables.source: Derived: Sentinel-1 flood (flood_s1_pipeline.py) x WorldPop R2025A 1 km / oil wells & fields (OSM, GEM GOGET); scripts/flood_exposure.py
variables.label_original: Oil wells/fields in or within 1 km of flood water
variables.plain: Number of mapped oil wells or fields with flood water within 1 km. A warning sign for possible oil pollution spread, not a measure of it.
variables.method: Count of OSM wells / GEM GOGET fields within 1 km of Sentinel-1 flood pixels.
variables.caution: Exposure only, not measured contamination. Well mapping is incomplete (mostly Rubkona/Guit).

variables.label: Open water (radar)
variables.aggregation: open-water share of known area x county area
variables.notes: Dark, specular open water (rivers, lakes, open flood water). Wind-roughened water is missed; dry sandy/clay surfaces rarely reach these thresholds. Radar (C-band SAR) change detection on a ~440 m grid (10 m scenes read at 160 m, block-averaged): a pixel is FLOODED when its monthly mean VV-VH ratio is > 3.0 dB above its own dry-season reference (median of the March means 2018-2025) - water under grass/papyrus/rice produces a double bounce that brightens VV much more than VH; OPEN WATER = VV < -18 and VH < -24 dB. Sees through cloud (unlike MODIS) and sees water under vegetation, which is most of the Sudd flood. It measures inundation BEYOND the normal dry-season state: permanent swamp is part of the reference and is not counted, so values are near 0 in the dry season. Validated on 4-8 Oct 2022 UNOSAT (new flood vs March 2022: F1 0.59, area ratio 0.95; see docs/CLIMATE_DATA_DECISIONS.md). Revisit 6-12 days 2018-2021, 12-24 days after Sentinel-1B failed (Dec 2021) until Sentinel-1C (2025): pixels without an acquisition inherit the previous month (max 2); county-months with <50% known area dropped.
variables.source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 A/B IW GRD, radiometrically terrain-corrected (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Area of open, calm water (rivers, lakes, open flood water) in square kilometres, mapped by radar satellite.
variables.method: Sentinel-1 pixels with VV < -18 dB and VH < -24 dB (dark, mirror-like water).
variables.caution: Jumps about 10x in 2025 from satellite and processing changes: not safe for trends. Wind-roughened water is missed.

variables.label: People living in flooded areas
variables.aggregation: sum over 1 km cells of population x flooded fraction (scaled up if <100% of the county observed)
variables.notes: Faecal-contamination exposure: about half of households practise open defecation (ISNA 2022-24) and pit latrines flood, so people in flooded cells are exposed to contaminated water (cholera, AWD, hepatitis E). WorldPop places people on their usual settlements; displaced people and dyke-protected towns (Bentiu, Rubkona) are not modelled. Exposure, not measured contamination: no open county-level water-quality data exist for South Sudan. Flood = Sentinel-1 flooded class (VV-VH rise >3 dB over the March reference; reliable Jul-Nov, under-detects receding Dec-Jun water).
variables.source: Derived: Sentinel-1 flood (flood_s1_pipeline.py) x WorldPop R2025A 1 km / oil wells & fields (OSM, GEM GOGET); scripts/flood_exposure.py
variables.plain: Estimated number of people whose homes are in places the radar map shows as flooded. Floods mix with latrine waste, so this signals exposure to contaminated water.
variables.method: Sentinel-1 flood class x WorldPop R2025A 1 km population (year-matched).
variables.caution: Exposure, not illness. Misses displaced people and dyke-protected towns (Bentiu, Rubkona); radar misses dry-season water.

variables.label: Radar flood map: coverage in month
variables.aggregation: share of county area with >=1 acquisition in the month
variables.notes: Quality flag for flood_s1_*; drops after Sentinel-1B failure (Dec 2021).
variables.source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 A/B IW GRD, radiometrically terrain-corrected (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Data-quality check for the radar flood layer: share of the county covered by satellite passes that month. Drops after one of the two satellites failed in Dec 2021.
variables.method: Share of county area with a Sentinel-1 acquisition (or carried value) in the month.
variables.how_to_read: Low = radar flood value is less reliable

variables.label: Share of people living in flooded areas
variables.aggregation: flood_population_exposed / WorldPop county total x 100
variables.notes: See flood_population_exposed. Exposure, not measured contamination: no open county-level water-quality data exist for South Sudan. Flood = Sentinel-1 flooded class (VV-VH rise >3 dB over the March reference; reliable Jul-Nov, under-detects receding Dec-Jun water).
variables.source: Derived: Sentinel-1 flood (flood_s1_pipeline.py) x WorldPop R2025A 1 km / oil wells & fields (OSM, GEM GOGET); scripts/flood_exposure.py
variables.label_original: Share of population in flooded areas
variables.plain: Percentage of the county's population whose homes are in places the radar map shows as flooded.
variables.method: Sentinel-1 flood class x WorldPop R2025A 1 km population, divided by county population.
variables.caution: Exposure, not illness. Misses displaced people and dyke-protected towns; radar misses dry-season water.

variables.label: Sudd flooded area incl. swamp
variables.aggregation: sum of inundated pixel area (observed + carried + climatology probability), day-weighted monthly mean of 8-day composites
variables.notes: Sudd counties only (16). Per 8-day MOD09A1 composite, QA-clear pixels (state flags + blue<0.2) are classed OPEN WATER if MNDWI(b4,b6)>0 and INUNDATED if open water or EVI-LSWI<=0.05 (Xiao et al. 2006 / Sakamoto et al. 2007 flooding signal; captures water under papyrus/grass that MNDWI misses). Cloudy pixels take their last clear state if <=3 composites (24 days) old, else the 2018-2025 probability of inundation for that composite-of-year. Monthly = day-weighted mean of the 8-day areas. Sep-Oct 2022 partly from MCD43A4 NBAR (Terra tiles missing on PC). 2025-07..2025-11 missing (no MODIS on PC). Validation: docs/VALIDATION_sudd_water.md.
variables.source: NASA MODIS Terra MOD09A1 v061 8-day 500 m surface reflectance via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.label_original: Sudd inundated area incl. flooded vegetation (MODIS)
variables.plain: Area under water, including water hidden under swamp grass and papyrus, in square kilometres. Our most consistent all-season flood record for the 16 Sudd counties.
variables.method: MODIS MOD09A1 8-day 500 m: open water (MNDWI > 0) or flooded vegetation (EVI-LSWI <= 0.05); validated vs UNOSAT (ratio 0.99).
variables.caution: Sudd counties only. Jul-Nov 2025 missing (no satellite data). Dense papyrus is missed in the dry season.

variables.label: Sudd flooded area incl. swamp (% of county)
variables.aggregation: sudd_inundation_km2 / county area x 100
variables.notes: Sudd counties only (16). Per 8-day MOD09A1 composite, QA-clear pixels (state flags + blue<0.2) are classed OPEN WATER if MNDWI(b4,b6)>0 and INUNDATED if open water or EVI-LSWI<=0.05 (Xiao et al. 2006 / Sakamoto et al. 2007 flooding signal; captures water under papyrus/grass that MNDWI misses). Cloudy pixels take their last clear state if <=3 composites (24 days) old, else the 2018-2025 probability of inundation for that composite-of-year. Monthly = day-weighted mean of the 8-day areas. variables.label_original: Sudd inundated area (% of county, MODIS)
variables.plain: Share of the county under water, including water hidden under swamp grass and papyrus. Covers only the 16 Sudd wetland counties.
variables.method: MODIS MOD09A1 8-day 500 m: open water (MNDWI > 0) or flooded vegetation (EVI-LSWI <= 0.05); cloud gaps filled.
variables.caution: Sudd counties only. July-November 2025 is missing. Dense papyrus is missed in the dry season.

variables.label: Sudd open water (no vegetation)
variables.aggregation: sum of open-water pixel area (MNDWI>0), day-weighted monthly mean of 8-day composites
variables.notes: Open water only (MNDWI>0); small (100s-1000s km2) and zero in some counties, so index_ok false. Sudd counties only (16). Per 8-day MOD09A1 composite, QA-clear pixels (state flags + blue<0.2) are classed OPEN WATER if MNDWI(b4,b6)>0 and INUNDATED if open water or EVI-LSWI<=0.05 (Xiao et al. 2006 / Sakamoto et al. 2007 flooding signal; captures water under papyrus/grass that MNDWI misses). variables.source: NASA MODIS Terra MOD09A1 v061 8-day 500 m surface reflectance via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Area of open water with no plants on top (rivers, lakes, flood lakes) in square kilometres, in the 16 Sudd counties.
variables.method: MODIS MOD09A1 8-day 500 m pixels with MNDWI > 0.
variables.caution: Small and zero in some counties; most Sudd water stands under vegetation, so see the Sudd flooded-area layer.

variables.label: Sudd water map: directly observed share
variables.aggregation: day-weighted mean share of county pixels observed clear in the 8-day composites
variables.notes: Quality flag: share of the value that is directly observed (the rest is gap-filled). Low Jun-Oct.
variables.source: NASA MODIS Terra MOD09A1 v061 8-day 500 m surface reflectance via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Data-quality check for the Sudd water layer: share of the value seen directly by the satellite rather than filled in. Low from June to October.
variables.method: Share of the county's monthly value from QA-clear MODIS observations (rest carried forward or climatology).
variables.how_to_read: Low = more of the value is estimated

variables.label: Sudd water map: share estimated from typical years
variables.aggregation: day-weighted mean share of county pixels filled from the 2018-2025 composite climatology
variables.notes: Quality flag: pixels cloudy for >24 days, filled with their 2018-2025 inundation probability for that time of year; high values pull the month toward the climatological mean.
variables.source: NASA MODIS Terra MOD09A1 v061 8-day 500 m surface reflectance via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Data-quality check for the Sudd water layer: share of the county that was cloudy too long and was filled with the usual value for that time of year.
variables.method: Share of pixels cloudy >24 days, filled with their 2018-2025 inundation probability for that composite of the year.
variables.how_to_read: High = the month's value leans toward the long-term average

variables.label: Surface water (% of county)
variables.aggregation: water pixels / known (observed or gap-filled) pixels x 100
variables.notes: Water = MNDWI (B4 green vs B7 SWIR 2.1um) > 0.1 in >=50% of cloud-free 8-day composites in the month (Terra+Aqua). Captures open water and shallow inundation; some residual false positives from dark wet vegetation early in the wet season (Jun-Aug). Cloud gaps filled from previous month (max 2 months); county-months with <20% known area dropped. Detects open water; under-detects flooded/floating vegetation (Sudd) and is reduced by persistent wet-season cloud. Validation vs 30 UNOSAT VIIRS water-extent tables (HDX, 2022-10..2025-04, scripts/water_validate_unosat.py): state-level r = 0.76; MODIS totals ~0.5x UNOSAT (close in Jun-Sep, 2-5x lower in the dry season when UNOSAT counts vegetated swamp water). Treat as a conservative, relative flood signal.
variables.source: MODIS MOD09A1 + MYD09A1 v061 8-day surface reflectance via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Share of the county covered by visible water (rivers, lakes, open flood water) in the month, seen by NASA's MODIS satellites. Works in all seasons.
variables.method: MODIS Terra+Aqua 8-day: MNDWI(B4,B7) > 0.1 in at least half of cloud-free composites; cloud gaps carried up to 2 months.
variables.caution: Misses water under vegetation and is blocked by rainy-season cloud; totals are about half of UNOSAT maps. Read as a relative signal.

variables.label: Surface water area
variables.aggregation: water share of known pixels x county area
variables.notes: Water = MNDWI (B4 green vs B7 SWIR 2.1um) > 0.1 in >=50% of cloud-free 8-day composites in the month (Terra+Aqua). Captures open water and shallow inundation; some residual false positives from dark wet vegetation early in the wet season (Jun-Aug). Cloud gaps filled from previous month (max 2 months); county-months with <20% known area dropped. Detects open water; under-detects flooded/floating vegetation (Sudd) and is reduced by persistent wet-season cloud. Validation vs 30 UNOSAT VIIRS water-extent tables (HDX, 2022-10..2025-04, scripts/water_validate_unosat.py): state-level r = 0.76; MODIS totals ~0.5x UNOSAT (close in Jun-Sep, 2-5x lower in the dry season when UNOSAT counts vegetated swamp water). Treat as a conservative, relative flood signal.
variables.source: MODIS MOD09A1 + MYD09A1 v061 8-day surface reflectance via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Area covered by visible water (rivers, lakes, open flood water) in square kilometres, seen by NASA's MODIS satellites. Works in all seasons.
variables.method: MODIS Terra+Aqua 8-day: MNDWI(B4,B7) > 0.1 in at least half of cloud-free composites; cloud gaps carried up to 2 months.
variables.caution: Misses water under vegetation and is blocked by rainy-season cloud; totals are about half of UNOSAT maps. Read as a relative signal.

variables.label: Surface-water map: cloud-free coverage
variables.aggregation: share of county pixels with >=1 clear 8-day observation
variables.notes: Data-quality flag for surface_water_*; low in wet season (Jun-Oct).
variables.source: MODIS MOD09A1 + MYD09A1 v061 8-day surface reflectance via Microsoft Planetary Computer
variables.plain: Data-quality check for the surface-water layer: share of the county the satellite could see through clouds that month. Low in the rainy season (Jun-Oct).
variables.method: Share of county area with cloud-free MODIS 8-day observations in the month.
variables.how_to_read: Low = surface-water value is less reliable that month

variables.source: Derived from the Sudd MODIS water index (MOD09A1, Planetary Computer)
variables.aggregation: inundated area minus open-water area per county-month (gap-filled 8-day composites)
variables.label: Flooded vegetation, Sudd (% of county)
variables.notes: Flooded vegetation as a share of the county's area.
variables.plain: Share of the county covered by swamp or grassland standing in water. Radar and plain water maps often miss this kind of flooding.
variables.method: MODIS 8-day inundation (incl. flooded vegetation, Xiao/Sakamoto rule) minus open water (MNDWI > 0); cloudy pixels gap-filled.
variables.how_to_read: Higher = more swamp under water.

variables.source: Derived from the Sudd MODIS water index (MOD09A1, Planetary Computer)
variables.aggregation: inundated area minus open-water area per county-month (gap-filled 8-day composites)
variables.label: Flooded vegetation, Sudd (km²)
variables.notes: Swamp and grassland standing in water (papyrus, reeds, flooded grass). Radar and plain water maps often miss it.
variables.plain: Area of swamp and grassland standing in water (papyrus, reeds, flooded grass) in Sudd counties. Radar and plain water maps often miss this kind of flooding.
variables.method: MODIS 8-day inundation (incl. flooded vegetation, Xiao/Sakamoto rule) minus open water (MNDWI > 0); cloudy pixels gap-filled.
variables.how_to_read: Higher = more swamp under water.

variables.label: Evaporation demand (TerraClimate)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS
variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of 1/24° cells (cell coverage fraction x cos lat)
variables.plain: How much water the air could evaporate from wet ground and plants in the month, given heat, sun, wind and humidity. Higher = thirstier conditions.
variables.method: TerraClimate reference evapotranspiration (Penman-Monteith), mm/month.

variables.aggregation: county mean as computed in Drive pipeline (POWER grid cells averaged over county)
variables.label: Evaporation demand (simple estimate)
variables.source: Derived (Thornthwaite) from MERRA-2 T2M via NASA POWER
variables.notes: Computed by the team from monthly mean temperature.
variables.plain: How much water the air could evaporate from wet ground and plants in the month, based on temperature only. Higher = thirstier conditions.
variables.method: Thornthwaite potential evapotranspiration from MERRA-2 monthly mean temperature.
variables.caution: This simple formula underestimates evaporation in hot, dry climates; prefer the Penman-Monteith version for size.

variables.label: Runoff (TerraClimate)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS
variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of 1/24° cells (cell coverage fraction x cos lat)
variables.notes: Often 0 in the dry season, so ratio to 2018 can be undefined. Coverage 2018-01..2025-12.
variables.plain: Rain water that runs off the land into streams in the month, in millimetres. Often zero in the dry season.
variables.method: TerraClimate water-balance runoff (mm/month).
variables.caution: Understated because TerraClimate rain is dry-biased after 2018.

variables.label: Water shortfall for plants (climatic water deficit)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS
variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of 1/24° cells (cell coverage fraction x cos lat)
variables.notes: PET minus AET; 0 when demand is fully met, so ratio to 2018 can be undefined. Coverage 2018-01..2025-12.
variables.plain: How much more water plants and soil could have used than was available in the month, in millimetres. Higher = drier conditions.
variables.method: TerraClimate potential minus actual evapotranspiration (mm/month).
variables.caution: Overstated because TerraClimate rain is dry-biased after 2018.

variables.label: Water used by plants and soil (TerraClimate)
variables.source: TerraClimate v1.1 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) via NKN THREDDS
variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of 1/24° cells (cell coverage fraction x cos lat)
variables.notes: Water actually evaporated/transpired; tracks vegetation water use. Coverage 2018-01..2025-12.
variables.plain: Water that actually evaporated from soil and plants in the month, in millimetres. Tracks how much water vegetation is using.
variables.method: TerraClimate actual evapotranspiration (water-balance model).
variables.caution: TerraClimate runs about 40% drier than other rain products in 2018-2025, so it leans toward drought.

variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of grid cells inside the county (0.05° resampling)
variables.label: Groundwater
variables.source: G3P v1.12 Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product, GFZ (DOI 10.5880/G3P.2024.001)
variables.notes: GRACE total storage minus modelled soil moisture, surface water, snow and glaciers, vs the 2002–2020 mean. Ends Sep 2023 (latest G3P release). In the Sudd, errors in the surface-water term can leak into this series; treat it as indicative. No data Jan–May 2018.
variables.plain: Whether groundwater is above or below its 2002-2020 average, in centimetres of water, from the GRACE and GRACE-FO gravity satellites with soil moisture, surface water and snow removed.
variables.method: G3P v1.12: GRACE total water storage minus modelled soil moisture and surface water, vs 2002-2020 mean.
variables.how_to_read: Above 0 = more groundwater than average; below 0 = less
variables.caution: Ends September 2023. Less conclusive in and around the Sudd wetland, where flood water on the surface can be mistaken for groundwater (hatched counties). NASA's GLDAS groundwater product will replace this once Google Earth Engine access is set up.

variables.label: Groundwater
variables.source: NASA GLDAS-2.2 Catchment Land Surface Model with GRACE/GRACE-FO data assimilation (GLDAS_CLSM025_DA1_D v2.2, band GWS_tavg) via Google Earth Engine (NASA/GLDAS/V022/CLSM/G025/DA1D)
variables.native_resolution: 0.25° (~28 km) model grid; GRACE information it assimilates is ~300 km
variables.aggregation: per-pixel monthly mean of daily groundwater storage minus the pixel's 2004-2020 mean, in cm; then mean of ~1 km cells inside the county
variables.notes: Groundwater only: the Catchment model splits the GRACE total-storage signal into soil moisture, snow and groundwater, and this is the groundwater part, as a difference (cm of water) from its own 2004-2020 average. Negative = less groundwater than usual. The model is nudged toward GRACE, so the detail finer than ~300 km comes from the model and its rainfall forcing, not from the satellite. Less conclusive in and around the Sudd wetland, where flood water on the surface can be mistaken for groundwater.
variables.plain: Groundwater compared with its 2004–2020 average, in centimetres of water, from NASA's GLDAS-2.2 land model, which takes in GRACE and GRACE-FO satellite gravity data.
variables.caution: The GRACE signal the model takes in is about 300 km wide, so neighbouring counties move together. Less conclusive in and around the Sudd wetland, where flood water on the surface can be mistaken for groundwater (hatched counties).

variables.label: Groundwater
variables.source: NASA GSFC / NDMC GRACE-based global drought indicators (GRACEDADM_CLSM025_GL_7D, gws_inst): Catchment land surface model with GRACE/GRACE-FO data assimilation
variables.native_resolution: 0.25° (~28 km) model grid; GRACE information it assimilates is ~300 km
variables.aggregation: per-pixel mean of the weekly percentiles dated in the month, then mean of ~1 km cells inside the county
variables.notes: Groundwater only. Each week the model's groundwater storage is ranked against its own long-term record for the same time of year: 50 = normal, below 20 = unusually dry (drought), above 80 = unusually wet. It is a ranking, not an amount of water, so compare counties by how far they are from 50, not as cm. In South Sudan the values sit low for the whole period (national mean ~4 in 2018, ~20-36 in 2020-2025), i.e. the model places 2018-2025 groundwater below its long-term norm; read the change over time and differences between counties rather than the absolute level. Same NASA system as GLDAS-2.2 CLSM GRACE-DA; the GRACE signal it assimilates is ~300 km wide, so neighbouring counties move together. No data for 2025-10 (weekly updates paused Oct-Nov 2025). Less conclusive in and around the Sudd wetland, where flood water on the surface can be mistaken for groundwater.
variables.label_original: Groundwater drought indicator (NASA GRACE data assimilation)
variables.plain: Groundwater compared with its long-term normal for the time of year, as a percentile. 50 is normal, below 20 is unusually dry and above 80 is unusually wet. The values come from NASA's land model, which assimilates GRACE and GRACE-FO satellite gravity data.
variables.caution: This is a ranking, not an amount of water. South Sudan is below its long-term normal for the whole period, so look at the change over time. Readings in and around the Sudd wetland (hatched counties) are less certain, because surface flood water can be mistaken for groundwater. October 2025 is missing.

variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of grid cells inside the county (0.05° resampling)
variables.label: Groundwater estimate: uncertainty
variables.source: G3P v1.12 (uncertainty)
variables.notes: One-standard-deviation uncertainty of the groundwater anomaly.
variables.plain: How uncertain the satellite groundwater estimate is, in centimetres of water. Larger = less confident.
variables.method: G3P v1.12 one-standard-deviation uncertainty of the groundwater storage anomaly.

variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of grid cells inside the county (0.05° resampling)
variables.label: Total water stored in the land (satellite gravity)
variables.source: GFZ GravIS COST-G combined GRACE/GRACE-FO Level-3 TWS (DOI 10.5880/COST-G.GRAVIS_02_L3_TWS)
variables.notes: All water on and below the land surface (surface water, soil moisture, groundwater) relative to the 2002–2020 mean. ~300 km effective resolution: neighbouring counties share most of the signal, so read it regionally (e.g. the Sudd). No data Jan–May 2018 (gap between GRACE and GRACE-FO), so the 2018 baseline is Jun–Dec only. High values in the Sudd mostly reflect flood water, not groundwater.
variables.plain: All water on and under the ground (floods, soil, groundwater) compared with the 2002-2020 average, in centimetres.
variables.method: GFZ GravIS COST-G combined GRACE/GRACE-FO Level-3 terrestrial water storage anomaly.
variables.caution: About 300 km resolution: read regionally, not county by county. No data Jan-May and Aug-Sep 2018. Sudd highs mostly reflect flood water.

variables.aggregation: area-weighted mean of grid cells inside the county (0.05° resampling)
variables.label: Water storage estimate: uncertainty
variables.source: GFZ GravIS COST-G Level-3 TWS (std_tws)
variables.notes: One-standard-deviation uncertainty of the storage anomaly.
variables.plain: How uncertain the satellite water-storage estimate is, in centimetres of water. Larger = less confident.
variables.method: GFZ GravIS COST-G one-standard-deviation uncertainty (std_tws).

variables.label: Strongest wind of the month
variables.source: MERRA-2 via NASA POWER (parameter WS10M_MAX)
variables.aggregation: value of the POWER grid cell containing the county centroid (centroid sampling; grid cells are ~county-sized or larger)
variables.notes: Maximum hourly 10 m wind speed in the month (storm/dust-wind proxy).
variables.plain: Highest hourly wind speed at 10 m height during the month, in metres per second. A rough signal of storms and dust-raising winds.

variables.label: Households feeling unsafe fetching water
variables.notes: A household member felt unsafe while collecting water (recall 2 weeks in 2023-24). Water collection is done mostly by women and girls, so this is a GBV-exposure proxy. Household survey, Jul-Sep each year (shown at YYYY-07). Rounds 2022-2024 only: no county-level MSNA tables exist on HDX for 2018-2021, so the baseline is 2022. Questions were reworded between rounds (e.g. 2022 groups shallow wells with rivers/ponds), so small year-to-year changes are not meaningful; county samples are ~100-300 households (margin of error ~5-10 points).
variables.source: South Sudan Inter-Sector Needs Assessment (ISNA, the country's MSNA; REACH/IMPACT for OCHA & ICCG) 2022-2024, county tables on HDX
variables.aggregation: weighted % of surveyed households in county (all population groups)
variables.label_original: Households feeling unsafe while collecting water
variables.plain: Share of households where someone felt unsafe while collecting water. Women and girls do most water collection, so this signals risk of violence against them.
variables.method: South Sudan Inter-Sector Needs Assessment (ISNA, REACH/IMPACT for OCHA), household survey Jul-Sep, county tables 2022-2024. Two-week recall in 2023-24.
variables.caution: Measures risk, not actual incidents. Only 2022, 2023 and 2024; question wording changed between rounds.

variables.aggregation: weighted % of surveyed households in county (all population groups)

variables.caution: Measures risk, not actual incidents. Only 2022, 2023 and 2024; question wording changed between rounds.
